note: What the manufacturer's own documentation says about the console's memory timing, and what this project derives from it. Every figure here is either quoted from the document named below or shown as arithmetic on figures that are. This file is the authority on the numbers the layout module counts in. When an implementation disagrees with it, the implementation is wrong.

order: hardware.json, for anything Nintendo printed and anything that follows from it by arithmetic shown here
the corpus, for header combinations read out of real cartridges
neither overrides the other, because they answer different questions
authority.why: The access-cycle counts every emulator uses are correct, but an emulator is not why they are correct. All three follow from the speeds the manual prints, two in the Map Mode table and the third in section 21.1, and Figure 2-21-1 says which addresses run at which.

comparedAgainst.what: The headers of every retail cartridge in a real library, which is the artifact rather than a description of it.

busSpeeds.note: These are the two speeds a cartridge selects between in its header, row 20H and row 30H of the table. Both of this project's cartridge access counts follow from them.

cpuClockSpeeds.quote: Three clock speeds are available: 3.58MHz, 2.68MHz, and 1.79 MHz.
cpuClockSpeeds.note: The text layer prints the third as 1 .79 MHz. The page image of printed page 2-21-1 reads 1.79 MHz, and the flattened text the checker compares is the same either way.

cpuMemoryMap.section: Figure 2-21-1, Super NES CPU Memory Map, printed page 2-21-2
cpuMemoryMap.readFrom: The page image only, because the text layer carries the caption and none of the figure. Rendered at 110 and again at 250 dots per inch, cropped to the address legend; both readings agree. The rows are the legend beside banks 00 to 3F; the columns for banks 80 to BF carry the same divisions.

masterClockHz.derivation: Six times the NTSC colour carrier, 3579545.4545 Hz, rounded to the nearest hertz. The console counts in this.
masterClockHz.note: Not from Book I. It is the standard NTSC relationship, and it is what makes the arithmetic below come out whole.

fastAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477272 / 3.58 MHz = 5.9992, so six master cycles, and six master cycles back the other way is 3.5795 MHz, which is the 3.58 MHz the manual prints.
fastAccessMasterCycles.note: Derived from a documented figure rather than taken from an implementation. The rounding is in the manual's own printing of the speed, not in this.

slowAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477272 / 2.68 MHz = 8.0139, so eight master cycles, and eight master cycles back the other way is 2.6847 MHz, which the manual prints as 2.68 MHz.

extraSlowAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477273 / 1.79 MHz = 11.998, so twelve master cycles, and twelve master cycles back the other way is 1.7898 MHz, which the manual prints as 1.79 MHz.
extraSlowAccessMasterCycles.note: Derived from the third speed section 21.1 prints, for the region Figure 2-21-1 labels CONTROLLER.

sa1BankSwitching.quote: The entire mask ROM is divided into 8 Mbit blocks, which can be projected onto the 8 Mbit areas, 0000H-FFFFH in banks C0H-CFH, D0H-DFH, E0H-EFH, and F0H-FFH.

sa1RomProjection.quote: The ROM data in banks CXH, DXH, EXH, and FXH, described above, is image projected onto, respectively, the 8 Mbit area 8000H-FFFFH, in banks 00H-1FH, 20H-3FH, 80H-9FH, and A0H-BFH.

sa1RomOrder.quote: The image projection method used is different from that used in Map Mode 21 in that the ROM data is projected in successive order, as demonstrated below. C0:0000H~C0:7FFFH -> 00:8000H~00:FFFFH C0:8000H~C0:FFFFH -> 01:8000H~01:FFFFH

sa1FirstBlocks.quote: It is also possible to project the first 8 Mbits of data in the mask ROM (00:0000H~0F:FFFFH) onto bank 00H-1FH, regardless of the settings for banks CXH, DXH, EXH, and FXH. In a similar manner, data in 10:0000H~1F:FFFFH, 20:0000H~2F:FFFFH, and 30:0000H~3F:FFFFH can be projected onto banks 20H-3FH, 80H-9FH, and A0H-BFH, respectively.

sa1BackupRamBanks.quote: Backup RAM is assigned to areas in bank 40H, justified to 0000H

sa1BackupRamImage.quote: Backup RAM is image projected to the 64 Kbit areas in 6000H-7FFFH of banks 00H-3FH and 80H-BFH.

sa1Registers.quote: The Super MMC control registers are assigned to 2200H-23FFH of banks 00H-3FH and 80H-BFH.

sa1Iram.quote: The I-RAM is assigned to 3000H-37FFH in banks 00H-3FH and 80H-BFH during Super NES CPU access
sa1Iram.note: The text layer prints l-RAM, a recogniser's reading of I-RAM; the page image reads I-RAM.

sa1Vectors.quote: Set the address for the Super NES CPU vectors and ROM-registered data to 00:7FB0H~00:7FFFH. When set to this area, they are assigned to FFB0H-FFFFH in bank 00H at Super NES start-up.

sa1NoHighSpeed.quote: The SAS cannot use the Super NES CPU high-speed mode (3.58 MHz).
sa1NoHighSpeed.note: The console still decides the speed from the address, as Figure 2-21-1 of Book I prints it; this is why the SA-1 mapping byte is 23H and never 33H.
sa1NoHighSpeed.unreachable: A rule for the program rather than for the map. The console decides the speed of an access from its address, as Figure 2-21-1 of Book I prints it, and nothing in a memory map can stop a program setting 420D; the header that a census reads carries 23H and never 33H, which the Map Mode table at page 1-2-17 of Book I also leaves out.

sa1Cxb.quote: SET SUPER MMC BANK C (CXB) Access: Super NES CPU Write Address: **2220H Size: 8 bits Initial value: 00H

sa1Dxb.quote: SET SUPER MMC BANK D (DXB) Access: Super NES CPU Write Address: **2221H Size: 8 bits Initial value: 01H

sa1Exb.quote: SET SUPER MMC BANK E (EXB) Access: Super NES CPU Write Address: **2222H Size: 8 bits Initial value: 02H

sa1Fxb.quote: SET SUPER MMC BANK F (FXB) Access: Super NES CPU Write Address: **2223H Size: 8 bits Initial value: 03H

sa1CxbFixed.quote: The game pak ROM area 1 is copied to addresses 8000H-FFFFH of banks 0XH-1XH.
sa1CxbFixed.note: The CBM bit, cleared by the initial value. The area is printed as a circled 1, which the text layer reads as a copyright sign.

sa1Bmaps.quote: SUPER NES CPU BW-RAM ADDRESS MAPPING (BMAPS) Access: Super NES CPU Write Address: **2224H Size: 8 bits Initial value: 00H

sa1Map.section: 3.1 Memory Map from Super NES CPU Perspective, Super NES Memory Map (SAS, Super NES CPU), printed page 1-3-1
sa1Map.readFrom: The page image only, because the text layer of this page is recognition noise. Rendered at 120 and again at 300 dots per inch, the page turned upright and cropped to each half; both readings agree. The bands between 2000H and 6000H are drawn to no scale, so the register and I-RAM pages are taken from sections 3.3.5 and 3.3.6.5 rather than from the drawing.

notCycleAccurate.note: What this project does and does not claim, so a reader does not inherit a stronger belief than the evidence supports.
notCycleAccurate.does: Reports how many master cycles an access to a resolved address costs, from the three speeds the manual prints.
doesNot: Model the CPU. How many accesses an instruction makes, and therefore what it costs, belongs to the processor rather than to the map.
Model refresh, DMA stalls, or the cycles the console spends on anything other than the access itself.

developmentManual.title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System Development Manual, Book I
developmentManual.note: Searched for a table of access cycles per region and for cycle counts in master clocks. It has neither. It prints three CPU clock speeds in section 21.1 and in Figure 2-21-1, and the two a cartridge selects in the Map Mode table, and that is enough for all three figures this project uses.
developmentManual.section: Map Mode table, page 1-2-17, and section 21.1, page 2-21-1
developmentManual.whatThatDigestIs: The copy this address served on 2026-08-27, fetched and held on the machine that records it. It identifies what was read rather than confirming it against an older pin, because no pin existed before: the figures had been read from a transcription at an archive with nothing on disk to hash. The two speeds and the Map Mode table were confirmed in the fetched copy, on the run of text that ends at printed page 1-2-17, which is where the record already said they sit.

notStated.what: The SPC7110 board's memory map, as resolve reads it for the spc7110 layout: registers at 4800 to 483F of banks 00 to 3F and 80 to BF, the decompression port in banks 50 and 58, backup RAM at 6000 to 7FFF, program ROM in the first megabyte of the image reached in banks 00 to 0F, 80 to 8F and C0 to CF, and data ROM after it in the other banks, at the bank registers' reset values, which give every data bank the data ROM's first megabyte.
notStated.source: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04: mia/Database/Super Famicom Boards.bml, boards SPC7110-RAM and SPC7110-RAM-EPSONRTC; ares/sfc/coprocessor/spc7110/spc7110.cpp, power() and mcuromRead(); ares/sfc/coprocessor/spc7110/data.cpp, dataromRead(); mia/medium/super-famicom.cpp, the program and data ROM split at 0x100000.
notStated.why: No Nintendo document known to exist prints the SPC7110 board, so this is an implementation's reading, cited as one. The header offset, FFC0, is the corpus's: all four retail SPC7110 cartridges carry it there.
notStated.howToSettleIt: The board's schematic, or a logic analyser on a cartridge: the chip select lines of the program and data ROMs for an access to each bank, and the bank registers 4830 to 4834 read back after a reset.

notStated.what: Where the SA-1 maps anything once a program writes its bank or backup RAM registers, 2220 to 2224. resolve answers for the initial values Book II prints, which is the map before the first write.
notStated.source: Book II prints both the registers and the map they select; this package keeps no register state, so it answers for one setting of them.
notStated.why: resolve is a question about an address and does not depend on anything having run, so the one map it can answer for is the one the initial values select.
notStated.howToSettleIt: Nothing here is unknown: Book II chapter 4 prints what each value selects. Modelling it needs a stateful map, which this package does not have.
